notes: Identity assessment: supplied publisher web parse identifies Policing and public health calls for service in Philadelphia, Jerry H. Ratcliffe, Crime Science 10, article 5 (2021), DOI 10.1186/s40163-021-00141-0, agreeing with the neutral original reference. Identified as Short Contribution and version of record dated 02 March 2021; primary report, not a secondary article or preregistration. Narrative sections through conclusion, references and author information are present. Table 1 has only its caption/Full size table link and Figures 1–4 only captions/Full size image links: their contents are not supplied. No PDF supplied or acquired. Target correspondence unresolved: broad description and empty locators cover multiple descriptive analyses. Candidate Table 1 N=1.07 million unique public-origin dispatched events is explicitly an analysis denominator, but is retained only as a candidate pending parent field-scope review. Nearly 80,000 medical/public-health calls are a subset, over 3.3 million are raw CAD entries, and over 13,000 are personnel shifts; these roles cannot be combined. No N arithmetic performed. Printed descriptive candidates: 7.4% of calls initially medical/public health; 8.6% of committed time for those calls; 54.7% of time for crime; nearly 80% of health calls retaining a health outcome; 11.6% of calls changing from health to other policing; 8.8% of events changing from non-health to health. These concern distinct outcomes/denominators and are not assigned as an effect size. No conversion performed. Narrative gives descriptive summaries rather than an identified inferential critical test or p-value. Missing table/figure contents preclude a source-wide absence claim. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
